query: For multicomponent high-entropy alloys in solid and liquid states at and near their high melting temperatures, what single testable methodological intervention could overcome the inability of EAM references to represent the many atomic configurations of the ab initio liquid? Explain why it should improve reference–target phase-space overlap, predict the reduction in thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD’s EAM references, define the applicable composition and temperature ranges, identify supporting evidence from elemental or binary calculations, and specify a decisive free-energy benchmark that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Replacing EAM references with a deep neural network potential trained on a broad sampling of ab initio liquid configurations will significantly improve phase‐space overlap and reduce the thermodynamic integration path mismatch in high-entropy alloy simulations at elevated temperatures.
generation.material_initial_state: Multicomponent high-entropy alloys in both solid and liquid states at and near their high melting temperatures.
generation.intervention: Develop and implement a deep neural network potential that is trained on diverse, ab initio liquid configurations to serve as the reference state in thermodynamic integration calculations.
generation.conditions: This method is applicable to refractory high-entropy alloys with complex chemical compositions near their melting points (e.g., temperatures exceeding 3000 K) where liquid-phase atomic diversity is particularly high.
generation.structural_mediator: The neural network potential mediates an improved representation of local atomic environments by capturing a broader spectrum of ab initio liquid configurations.
generation.mechanism: Because the DNN potential is trained on extensive ab initio data, it better captures the multitude of atomic configurations in the liquid, thereby enhancing phase‐space overlap with the target system and reducing the integration pathway mismatch relative to the limited configurational sampling provided by EAM potentials.
generation.predicted_outcome: A measurable reduction in the thermodynamic integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD’s EAM references with improved accuracy in free energy predictions of both liquid and solid states.
generation.baseline: Thermodynamic integration performed using TOR-TILD’s traditional EAM references, which do not capture the full diversity of atomic configurations in the ab initio liquid.
generation.boundary: The proposed intervention is expected to yield improvements mainly for multicomponent HEAs with significant atomic configurational complexity near high melting temperatures; the benefits may be less pronounced in simpler binary or mono-component alloys or at substantially lower temperatures.
generation.uncertainty: While preliminary insights suggest a potential improvement in reducing integration path mismatch on the order of 20–40%, the exact magnitude of improvement remains uncertain and must be empirically validated.

falsification_experiment.design: Conduct parallel thermodynamic integration studies on a representative high-entropy alloy system near its melting temperature. One study should use the traditional TOR-TILD EAM references and the other should use the proposed deep neural network potential as the reference. All simulation parameters, alloy compositions, and temperature conditions must be held constant.
measurements: Quantify and compare the thermodynamic integration path mismatches (e.g., cumulative free energy differences) between the two methods.
Evaluate phase-space overlap metrics via sampling of atomic configurations.
Validate free energy predictions against direct ab initio calculations or experimental melting temperature measurements.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the deep neural network potential does not result in a statistically significant reduction in the integration path mismatch and does not demonstrate improved phase-space overlap relative to the EAM reference, then the hypothesis will be falsified.

cited_evidence.text: AbstractThe efficient energy use in multiple sectors of modern industry is partly based on the efficient use of high-strength, high-performance alloys that retain remarkable mechanical properties at elevated and high temperatures. High-entropy alloys (HEAs) represent the most recent class of these materials with a high potential for high-temperature high-strength applications. Aside from their chemical composition and microstructure-property relationship, limited information on the effect of heat treatment as a decisive factor for alloy design is available in the literature. This work intends to contribute to this research topic by investigating the effect of heat treatment on the microstructure and mechanical performance of an Al4.4Co26Cr19Fe18Ni27Ti5.6 HEA. The solution annealed state is compared to aged states obtained at different heat treatment times at 750 °C. The temporal evolution of the matrix and the γ’-precipitates are analyzed in terms of chemical composition, crystallography, size, shape, and volume fraction by means of scanning electron microscopy, transmission electron microscopy, and atom probe tomography. The melting temperature is a crucial property of materials that determines their potential applications in different industrial fields. In this study, we used a deep neural network potential to describe the structure of high-entropy (TiZrTaHfNb)CxN1−x carbonitrides (HECN) in both solid and liquid states. This approach allows us to predict heating and cooling temperatures depending on the nitrogen content to determine the melting temperature and analyze structure changes from atomistic point of view. A steady increase in nitrogen content leads to increasing melting temperature, with a maximum approaching for 25% of nitrogen in the HECN. A careful analysis of pair correlations, together with calculations of entropy in the considered liquid phases of HECNs allows us to explain the origin of the nonlinear enhancement of the melting temperature with increasing nitrogen content. The maximum melting temperature of 3580 ± 30 K belongs to (TiZrTaHfNb)C0.75N0.25 composition. The improved melting behavior of high-entropy compounds by the addition of nitrogen provides a promising way towards modification of thermal properties of functional and constructional materials.

In fact, a statistical analysis of the AFLOW.org enthalpies indicates that the gain in formation enthalpy by adding mixing species, ΔHf(N + 1) − ΔHf(N), decreases with N, and can easily be overcome by the monotonic increase in entropy-gain for the disordered systems (to go from order to complete or partial disorder). In the AFLOW analysis, the threshold between low- and high-entropy systems is around four mixing species. To have completely entropy-stabilized materials, five mixing species are required (similar to the Entropy-Stabilized Oxides). For carbides in which only the metal-sublattice is randomly populated, five metals should be enough to achieve carbide entropy stabilization, especially at equi-composition. reading.lever: Replace EAM references with a deep neural network potential trained on diversified, ab initio liquid configurations.
reading.why: This intervention directly improves phase‐space overlap by capturing extensive atomic diversity in the liquid, reducing integration path mismatch versus TOR-TILD’s EAM.
